subject: Short-term region commitment and on-call SLA exception: clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term regional commitment and maintenance window handling

Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the call yesterday. We are close to finalizing platform selection, but two procurement items remain blockers for our InfoSec and Legal teams:

1) We need a commitment on region pinning for APAC customer workloads (primary placement in APAC) with a documented exception window for operator maintenance or capacity failures.
2) We need clarity on telemetry/analytics paths — specifically whether any aggregate analytics or monitoring telemetry will transit EU/US for processing and storage.

Attached: DPA_Addendum_Draft.pdf (redline we received from our counsel) and SOC2_summary.xlsx (requested control mapping).

Can you confirm:
- the maximum short-term cross-region processing window Redwood would expect for emergency failovers/maintenance,
- whether you can commit to a documented on-call escalation path and notification timeline, and
- what the subprocessor visibility and KMS custody model looks like for APAC pinning?

If easier, we can schedule a short ops + legal call next week.

Thanks,
Daniel
Security & Risk Lead
ClearPath Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term regional commitment and maintenance window handling

Daniel —

Appreciate the note and the attached doc. Short answers up front:
- Target: we can pin production workloads to APAC locations and provide a documented short-term failover window of up to 72 hours for operator-initiated maintenance or capacity-driven reroutes; we aim for 48 hours as the default operational tolerance and will surface exceptions beyond that.
- On-call / notifications: we will provide an escalation playbook (SLA notifications: 15m incident acknowledgement, 2h mitigation update, 24h post-incident report) and a named on-call contact during any planned maintenance that affects residency.
- Subprocessors & KMS: we can provide a subprocessor roster for the APAC region; KMS custody options include either Redwood-managed KMS (default) or customer-provided keys via KMS integration (bring-your-own-key). When customer keys are used, control-plane operations that require key access are limited and audited.

Notes / next steps:
- We should review the redline in your DPA addendum; Marissa (legal) is cc'd and will propose edits.
- For analytics telemetry: we treat aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry differently — we can restrict analytics processing to APAC by default, but some operational telemetry (paging/alert metrics) may transit to a central observability cluster during incidents unless isolated by contract. We can make isolation a contractual requirement if needed (adds operational constraints).

Proposed 30-min call: Mon 2026-11-23 10:00-10:30 PT (ops + legal + ClearPath security). If that works for you, I will send a calendar invite and an initial mutual action plan.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term regional commitment and maintenance window handling

Thanks, Neha. A few legal points to flag for clarity before the call:

1) DPA addendum redlines: please see attached DPA_addendum_redline.docx. We want to limit any cross-border processing to documented exceptions with an explicit approval flow (customer-authorized exception + notification cadence).
2) KMS and operator access: Daniel — can you confirm whether ClearPath requires HSM-backed keys or if cloud KMS (with customer-supplied keys) is sufficient for you? That will determine the exact escrow / access wording.
3) Subprocessor scope: we'll include cloud infra providers and CDN/observability providers in the subprocessor roster. For APAC residency, we need to indicate which subprocessors have access to unredacted customer data vs telemetry only.

Operational ask: can you share the types of telemetry you object to leaving APAC (e.g., raw logs, aggregated token-level metrics, alert traces)? We'll use that as our baseline for the contractual carve-outs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term regional commitment and maintenance window handling

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Notes / next steps:
> - For analytics telemetry: we treat aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry differently — we can restrict analytics processing to APAC by default, but some operational telemetry (paging/alert metrics) may transit to a central observability cluster during incidents unless isolated by contract.

Thanks — to be explicit: ClearPath will push for telemetry isolation that keeps any request/trace-level data and any user-derived embeddings inside APAC; aggregate counters and anonymized throughput metrics are acceptable to be shared outside APAC.

Procurement: we are OK with a 48h operational tolerance for emergency failover as long as there is a clear notification flow and a maximum cumulative annual exception cap (e.g., no more than 6 incidents per 12 months that exceed the region-binding). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept that cap as a contractual term.

Daniel

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@clearpathhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term regional commitment and maintenance window handling

Daniel —

Understood and thank you for the explicit bandwidth / cap ask. Confirmations and actionables below:

- Operational tolerance: Redwood can accept a default 48-hour short-term failover window for APAC pinning. For transparency, we will add language that allows exceptions up to 72 hours for operator escalation with documented approval.
- Annual cap: Redwood is willing to agree to a contractual cap of 6 cumulative incidents per 12-month period that result in region-binding exceptions, provided the incidents are categorized and reported (severity + root cause) and that the cap is subject to a materiality carve-out for force majeure and law enforcement obligations.
- Telemetry: we will update the DPA addendum to explicitly state that request/trace-level data and embeddings remain within APAC by default. Aggregated usage/throughput metrics and anonymized system telemetry may be processed in Redwood control-plane regions for monitoring unless customer selects telemetry isolation (add-on).
- KMS custody: we can offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for APAC tenancy; HSM option requires an enterprise addendum.

I'll send a calendar invite for Mon 2026-11-23 10:00 PT and a one-pager mutual action plan summarizing the items above and the draft DPA edits (DocuSign link included). Please review the DPA redline prior to the call.

Best,
Neha
Senior Product Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: DPA_addendum_redline.docx (from Marissa), DPA_Addendum_Draft.pdf, SOC2_summary.xlsx
